# v2.6.0 "Assay"

**The triangle, the noise channel and the sweep unit — and an audit of how much of the APU was fitted to the oracle rather than derived from documentation.**

An assay tests a metal to find out what it is actually made of. This release does that to rung 4 of the MiSTer co-simulation programme: for every APU behaviour in the SystemVerilog DUT, was it written from public hardware documentation, or tuned until it agreed with RustyNES? **The emulation core is untouched.**

---

## The audit, and why it exists

`docs/apu-oracle-vs-documentation.md` (in the sibling `RustyNES_MiSTer` repository) is the deliverable this release is named for. It catalogues every place the DUT follows the oracle rather than the NESdev wiki, sorted by risk, each with the documentation text it is measured against and the independent check that would adjudicate it.

It exists because **the oracle is an emulator, not silicon.** AccuracyCoin 141/141 is not "matches hardware". Rung 4's entire compare surface is oracle-defined, so a shared error between the two implementations is invisible to every gate **by construction** — the DUT was tuned until it agreed, and agreement with a wrong reference looks exactly like correctness.

The document is maintained going forward under one rule: **an item closes only when a gate exercises it *and* a mutation against it is CAUGHT.** A passing gate over an unexercised path is the precise thing it exists to track.

## The oracle passes blargg's APU battery, 29/29

Run for the first time in this programme:

| suite | result |
| --- | --- |
| `apu_test` | 8 / 8 |
| `apu_reset` | 6 / 6 |
| `apu_mixer` | 4 / 4 |
| `blargg_apu_2005` | 11 / 11 |

These are pass/fail ROMs written against real hardware, and the result is recorded **per audit item**, because it does not mean the same thing everywhere. For the `$4017` reset delay and the 5-step sequencer step it moved suspicion off the oracle entirely and onto the RTL.

Separately: the nineteen ROMs in `tests/roms/extra/apu` — including `apu_sweep_sub`, `apu_sweep_cutoff` and `apu_phase_reset`, whose names match the flagged paths exactly — are referenced by nothing and **cannot serve as gates**. Every one returns `status = 0` with an empty message; they are audio-output tests meant to be listened to. Recorded so nobody re-derives it from the filenames.

## The headline finding: two errors that were cancelling

v2.5.9 keyed the `$4017` reset delay on the **mode bit**. The wiki never mentions the mode bit — it keys the delay on the write's APU-cycle **parity**. That fit was exact *only* in combination with the 5-step sequencer's step 2 held one tick off the convention its fifteen siblings follow.

Measured across all eight APU ROMs:

| delay rule | 5-step step 2 | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| documented (fixed) | 7455 documented | **0 — exact** |
| documented (fixed) | 7456 fitted | 2, diverging **late** |
| mode-bit fitted | 7455 documented | 2, diverging **early** |
| mode-bit fitted | 7456 fitted | 0 — exact |

Two wrongs, one APU tick apart in opposite directions. The fitted rule was not merely unfalsified by the stimulus — it was **load-bearing for a second error**, which is why it survived both a mutation catalog and a documentation audit that looked directly at it.

Both documented values are adopted **because they are documented**, not because they fit better; both fit equally, and a fit was never the argument. All sixteen sequencer constants are now uniformly documented − 1 with nothing fitted, and reverting either half is a CAUGHT mutation.

The delay is now a **fixed** two APU ticks, with the documented 3-or-4 CPU-cycle split *emerging* from the countdown living inside `if (apu_phase)` rather than being written out a second time.

## Three unexercised paths gained gates; two found defects immediately

- **The sweep unit's period update was absent entirely.** That made `sweep_mutes` correct and untestable: a period nothing updates can never reach an overflowing target. `apusweep030` caught it at CPU cycle 47,853 on its first run.
- **No ROM had ever set the sweep negate bit**, so the documented pulse-1 one's-complement / pulse-2 two's-complement asymmetry had never executed. `apuneg033` configures both pulses identically *except which pulse they are*; they mute exactly one half-frame apart, as the one's complement predicts.
- **The frame IRQ window yielded two more defects.** The coincident-read rule was **inverted**, under a source comment asserting the ordering was correct: a `$4015` read landing on the assertion edge returned 0 *and* destroyed the assertion, where the wiki says such a read returns 1 and the flag survives. And the flag was asserted on only **one half** of its APU cycle, where the wiki lists both the GET and PUT halves.

`apuirq036` is the first rung-4 ROM gated on the **bus** rather than on channel levels, because the frame IRQ reaches the CPU and never the mixer. Its 11-cycle poll loop is the whole design: the obvious 10-cycle loop shares a factor with the 29,830-cycle sequence and would have read the same residue every frame forever, never once landing in the window, while looking entirely reasonable and passing.

## Two characterisations retracted

- **v2.5.9's residual was not a `$4003` write-parity sensitivity.** It was an inverted power-on APU tick parity plus a testbench that sampled channel levels one cycle early. Identified from the *shape* of the residual: all 5,076 remaining divergences satisfied `dut[c] == oracle[c-1]`, unanimously, and a per-channel bug cannot produce a unanimous one-cycle lag.
- **`apuquarter032`'s residual was not a rounding effect.** It had been described as a whole-cycle counter rounding half-APU-cycle steps. It was one sequencer constant off by one, and correcting it closed the residual with no change to any rounding logic. A residual small enough to look like rounding is exactly the size a single off-by-one produces.

## Verification

- **30 gates green across rungs 1–4**; **35 of 35 mutations CAUGHT**, 0 NOT CAUGHT, 0 BUILD-FAILED.
- **AccuracyCoin 141/141 (100.00%, RAM decoder)** and **nestest 0-diff**. The emulation core is untouched — the diff is the sibling DUT, the workspace-excluded `rustynes-cosim` crate, and documentation — so these hold **by construction**.

## Still open, and named

- Which APU phase the wiki's "during an APU cycle" refers to. Every `$4017` write in all eleven ROMs lands on the same phase, so an explicit parity rule measures byte-identically to the fixed constant now in the RTL.
- The inhibit term in `fc_irq_set_now`, which would make a `$4015` read return bit 6 spuriously while interrupts are inhibited. Closing it needs a bus-gated ROM that sets the inhibit bit while polling `$4015`.
